CHIEF COMPLAINT
Patient presents to discuss smoking cessation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old male with long-standing tobacco use presents motivated to quit smoking. Patient reports starting smoking in high school while experimenting with friends at parties. Over time, smoking became more regular and now smokes daily at 1.5 packs per day. Smokes first cigarette within one hour of waking. Patient has previously attempted to quit by going cold turkey approximately one year ago and was successful for almost a year. However, relapsed due to work-related stress, specifically layoffs at his workplace and increased work responsibilities. Patient reports recent motivation to quit stemming from becoming a father any day now with a daughter on the way. Patient has initiated stress management strategies including meditation and recently joined the gym. Friends have had success with nicotine patch, which patient is interested in using. Planned quit date is next Monday, which is also his birthday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not otherwise reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. Gout
3. History of 2/6 systolic murmur (previously discussed, currently monitored)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol for gout management

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a 44-year-old male with significant smoking history since high school. Currently smokes 1.5 packs per day. Works in industry experiencing workplace stress. Recently joined gym and has started meditation practice. About to become a father with daughter expected imminently. Married.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Blood pressure 128/88 mmHg, heart rate 68 bpm, respiratory rate 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm with 2/6 systolic murmur noted (previously known, stable).
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally. No expiratory wheezes, rales, or rhonchi appreciated.
Neck: No lymphadenopathy. No carotid bruits appreciated.

RESULTS
Vital signs as documented above. Physical examination findings as documented above. Hemoglobin A1c ordered for follow-up in two weeks.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Patient motivated to quit smoking with planned quit date of next Monday. Will initiate 21 mg nicotine patch on quit date. Patient counseled to change patch location daily to minimize skin irritation. Dosage will be decreased gradually over time with follow-up. Patient provided handouts regarding common smoking triggers. Encouraged to continue exercise routine, meditation, and consider yoga for stress management. Close monitoring of stress levels related to work and upcoming birth of child. Follow-up in two weeks to reassess and evaluate patch dosage.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Continue current management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c ordered and will be reviewed at two-week follow-up.

3. Gout: Continue allopurinol. Patient counseled to continue monitoring foods that exacerbate uric acid levels.

4. Follow-up appointment in two weeks.
